note: Adapted from Mjöberg's (1920) original description, originally in English (published under Hamitermes). The text is OCR from an Internet Archive scan, with some letters misread (e.g. seopulus = scopulus).

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Rather small, head very small, mandibles very short. Head distinctly longer than wide, the sides nearly parallel, the posterior margin rounded, pale yellow, with a whiter longitudinal patch in the middle; only the narrow short part of the clypeus visible, its anterior margin concave in the middle and bilobed, bearing 2 erect setae in the middle; labrum small, narrow at the base, inflated towards the apex; mandibles very short, incurved, very wide at the base, with a very obtuse median tooth near the middle; antennae pale yellow, the basal segment twice as long as wide and twice as long as segment 2, segment 3 extremely short (about one third of segment 2) and more or less fused with segment 4, segment 4 wider than segment 3; maxillary palps long and slender, distinctly longer than the mandibles. Measurements: body length with mandibles 4.1 mm; head length with mandibles 1.65 mm; head length without mandibles 1.44 mm; head width 1.06 mm; pronotum length 0.32 mm, width 0.67 mm; abdominal width 1.45 mm.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: White, head pale yellow. Head with a pale median line, paler anteriorly, the posterior margin and sides rounded, narrowed at the antennal sockets; clypeus with rounded raised sides, the apex small with a projecting point; labrum long and narrow, inflated towards the apex, the apex rounded and slightly concave; mandibles small, the left with 2 strong apical teeth, 1 sharp ridge and 1 angular process; the right with 2 broad lobate apical teeth and 1 larger rectangular tooth; antennae 15-segmented, segment 3 smallest and partly fused with segment 4. Measurements: body length 4 mm; head length 1.22 mm; head width 1.06 mm; pronotum length 0.32 mm, width 0.72 mm; abdominal width 1.39 mm.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: The shape of the head and the very short, stout mandibles with an obtuse median tooth make it very easy to recognize. The nest is characteristically a pointed cone about 1 m high and about 30 cm in diameter at the base, with a thin fragile grey outer covering and a system of galleries of the usual type inside. A neotenic queen is also described: body white, head pale yellow, eyes flat, antennae 15-segmented, body length 10 mm, abdominal width 2.50 mm.
